sealed.statement: PG wire owns one disable/prefer/require TLS policy: real PostgreSQL clients can authenticate and query through the production listener with a verified server certificate, require mode rejects plaintext downgrade before SQL, invalid certificate trust fails, and TLS key material remains outside runtime_config.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, independently verify every exact source attempt and the terminal aggregate with evidence subagent:verify_portability_plan.
The PG wire descriptor/runtime/protocol path owns disable, prefer, and require behavior; the example and client must not implement a second server-side policy.
Private keys, certificates, secure contexts, and certificate contents are composition-root inputs and must not be accepted in runtime_config or emitted in logs or errors.

The declared scenario uses the real pg client through createRuntimeStartupWiring and proves verified-TLS query success, plaintext downgrade rejection in require mode, and invalid-CA failure before SQL.
TLS does not widen explicit trust authentication; trust remains loopback-only and the externally deployable posture is password authentication with tlsMode require.
